lastCommit.message:
Visual language phase 2 — the third plane, the docked tab, and the lifted board

Phase 1 established the grammar and proved it on one screen. The Game Director
inspected it on the device and returned a verdict that separated the two
questions cleanly: *"THE GRAMMAR IS RIGHT. THE VISUAL SIGNAL IS TOO QUIET."*
So nothing here is a redesign. It is the same construction, made loud enough to
read at arm's length, and then propagated past the specimen.

TWO PLANES BECAME THREE, AND THAT IS THE WHOLE ANSWER TO "TOO QUIET".
Raising alpha again was ruled out by name in Phase 1 — past a point, more
contrast on a 1dp line is glow, not depth. The defect was that the sidewall sat
FLUSH against the dark rim, so the side of the key and the shadow beneath it
were the same line, and one line is an edge no matter how dark you make it. The
sidewall now runs 3dp and is LIFTED 1dp off the bottom, leaving room for a
near-black contact band underneath it. Top to bottom a chip reads

    lit rim · face light · FACE · SIDEWALL · CONTACT · dark rim

A side, and below it the dark where the object MEETS the surface it stands on.
The token values rose as well (face 0.16 → 0.30, sidewall 0.38 → 0.58) but the
geometry is what the eye is actually reading.

PRESSED IS NOW A GEOMETRY CHANGE, NOT A COLOUR SWAP. Owner: *"reduce apparent
height; compress/remove some lower sidewall; move the face toward the substrate;
reduce contact shadow… Opacity-only press feedback is insufficient."* On press
the sidewall COLLAPSES 3dp → 1dp, the contact band is not drawn at all — a key
pushed home is no longer standing on anything, and that absence IS the reduced
contact shadow — the shaded side moves above the face, and travel goes 1.5 → 2dp
because 1.5 was inside the noise on a dense row. The key visibly loses height.

THE TAB LANGUAGE, DEFERRED IN PHASE 1, IS IMPLEMENTED — AND NO CONSUMER MOVED.
Owner: *"NO arbitrary color-only selected state. Selected state must be
physically legible."* An INACTIVE tab wears the raised family's three planes and
stands proud of the row. An ACTIVE tab has no side and no contact at all, opens
its bottom border, and pushes `tabMouth` — its own material — 2dp PAST the row
baseline, so its body is continuous with the region it controls. Two objects,
not two colours: a key, and a key that has been pressed home.

The brief's drawing wants a panel with a visible top edge to dock INTO, and none
of TTabBar's three consumers render one. Rather than edit three screens, the
component owns the docking itself. `paddingBottom: 9` repays the 1dp the opened
border gives back, so the row's height cannot move. Crafting, Guidance and
Vendor are byte-identical.

A BOARD IS ABOVE THE GAME, AND UNTIL NOW IT DID NOT SAY SO. `modalCard` and
`momentCard` were a fill, a 1dp rim and a radius — the same construction as a
panel the player cannot touch. `boardLift` is shadow + elevation, and this is
the ONE place Android `elevation` is correct: the dossier construction refused
it because a four-sided halo is wrong on a compact chip standing on a plate, but
a board laid over the whole screen IS lifted on every side. Both are paint, so
all fourteen dialogs keep their exact geometry — asserted, not asserted-ish.

THE HEADER SEPARATES THE CONTROL FROM THE LABEL. Owner: *"BACK = interactive
physical control. TITLE = structural/read-only information."* BACK becomes a
render-prop Pressable carrying the full face/sidewall/contact construction and
collapsing under a thumb. The title deliberately gets nothing. Seven screens take
this header, so what BACK says about pressability is what most of Tartaria says.

WHAT THE GRAMMAR NOW REACHES, COUNTED
    tControlDepth ····· 61 call sites across 11 files   (2dp travel)
    tFilledGold ······· 13 further files                (same, via the above)
    TScreenHeader ····· 7 screens
    tModalCard ········ 19 call sites, 9 modals
    tMomentCard ······· 5 modals
    TTabBar ··········· 3 screens, zero consumer edits
    TButton/btnFace ··· 5 sites, 3 files
Ten lines of production code outside the kit. The rest is authority.

`btnFace` moved onto the chips' own tokens. It had carried `controlLit`/
`controlDark` since VIS-1, tuned when it was the only face treatment in the
game; beside chips drawing a 3dp side and a contact band, the one control that
was always the most physical had become the least.

STILL NO LAYOUT, WHICH IS STILL THE LICENCE. Every plane is an absolutely
positioned, `pointerEvents="none"` child inside a box the control already owns.
`boardLift` is shadow and elevation only — a test names 23 layout properties it
must not declare. 320×568 unchanged. The recess takes no raised plane, the
read-only frame takes none of it, and the chassis stays strictly shallower than
a command: same grammar, lower voice.

THE ENEMY CHAIN IS UNTOUCHED AND STILL ASSERTED. OTA-1514/arb146 records what a
new ancestor costs: the parent wins the responder on a vertical drag and the
card is capped with no way to scroll. ScrollView still owns the pan, the
Touchable still sits INSIDE it, the planes are inert children of the Touchable
that already owns the tap. The player panel keeps its whole-panel touch contract
and its `accessibilityLabel="Open player sheet"`, byte-identical.

NO NEW KIT EXPORT. 13/13 components, 10/10 helpers, 23/23 total, unmoved. Every
new style reaches its consumers as a `tartariaKitStyles` entry — the route
`panelFrame` takes.

EVIDENCE
  visualPhase2ThePhysicalPanel             30/30 (6 describes)
  23 negative controls, each applied → a NAMED guard red → restored
    byte-identical: sidewall deleted · contact removed · pressed stops
    collapsing · travel reverts to 1.5 · inactive tab goes flat · active tab
    loses its tongue · active tab keeps its border closed · dialogs lose
    elevation · boardLift grows a margin · header BACK loses its planes ·
    read-only frame takes the lift · input well grows a sidewall · card
    becomes as loud as a key · a second player-panel touch owner · a plane
    becomes interactive · the arb146 responder inversion · TButton drifts
    off-family · a nineteenth export · the phase leaks into the engine ·
    tModalCard drops the lift · tMomentCard drops the lift · the selected
    chip fill reverts to #221d15
  full required surface   1,298 suites · 13,974 tests (3 skipped) · 498.2 s
  22/22 check:* gates · typecheck:ci clean · typecheck:tests at baseline 201 ·
    lint clean · kit 13/13 · 10/10 · 23/23

THE FIRST FULL SURFACE WAS RED, AND MY OWN CONTROLS COULD NOT HAVE FOUND IT.
Three shipped suites, four assertions: OTA-1765's and OTA-1777's byte-for-byte
flatten pins broke on `boardLift`, and OTA-1776's whole-line `tabChipOn` pin
broke on the docking. Nineteen negative controls had all run against this pass's
own suite and the four it had amended, so none of them reached these. OTA-1776's
own header says exactly this in prose — *"the argument for running the whole
surface rather than the pass's own tests"* — and it was right.

None of the four was weakened. The flatten pins now assert the ORIGINAL geometry
byte-for-byte AND that the addition is exactly five paint keys AND that
`boardLift` declares none of 23 named layout properties; a future pass slipping a
margin into the lift fails even if it updated the literal. OTA-1776's pin moved
from a line spelling to the style block's actual fill and rim, which is what
DEFECT 3 was ever about. Four further negative controls prove none of the
amendments is vacuous.

A SUPERSEDED GUARD WAS REPLACED, NOT DELETED. OTA-1802's flat-tab assertion had
become VACUOUS: once the planes arrived as child Views rather than border
colours it would have passed on a fully raised tab. It is now a structural
contract on what a tab IS in both states.

OTA_BUILD_ID is NOT bumped by this commit. The device will still report
2026-09-11-1803; the identity of this build is its SHA.

Tests prove none of the aesthetics. Whether a chip now reads as a key, whether a
docked tab reads as engaged, whether a dialog reads as lifted — that is the
device and the owner's eye. This goes to the Golem development/test distribution
for exactly that.
